styles.name: Product Keynote Minimal
styles.description: One product claim per screen, held in a wide field of white with the interface itself as the only ornament.
styles.philosophy: A keynote works because it refuses to show two things at once. Every band states one idea, gives the product room to be looked at, and moves on.
dos: Give one claim the whole band
Let the product screenshot be the picture
donts: Never crowd two propositions into one band
Do not decorate what the product already shows

styles.name: Precision SaaS
styles.description: A tight, bordered grid where every claim is measurable and every surface has an edge you can see.
styles.philosophy: Trust in software is built from precision. Aligned edges, consistent rhythm and visible structure say the product was engineered by people who care about the same things.
dos: Keep every column edge on the same grid
donts: Never let a band float without an edge
Avoid photography where a diagram is truer

styles.name: Glass AI
styles.description: Layered translucent surfaces over a deep gradient field, with type that floats rather than sits.
styles.philosophy: Software that infers should feel like depth rather than paper. Stacked translucency suggests a system with layers you cannot see all of at once.
dos: Stack surfaces so depth reads as capability
Keep the accent for the one action that matters
donts: Never put a hard border on a glass surface
Do not let motion outlast the reading

styles.name: Technical Grid
styles.description: A blueprint sensibility: monospace labels, exposed grid lines and content that reads like documentation.
styles.philosophy: Some audiences are reassured by seeing the structure. The grid is not hidden behind the design — it is the design, annotated.

styles.name: Dark Product Lab
styles.description: A developer-console mood: near-black canvas, one signal colour and product surfaces lit from within.
styles.philosophy: The people who choose this product already work in the dark. The site should feel like the tool they will spend the day in, not the brochure about it.
dos: Show the product doing the work
Keep one signal colour and mean it
donts: Never brighten the canvas to sell to a non-technical buyer
Avoid stock photography of people at laptops

styles.name: Quiet Luxury
styles.description: Almost nothing on the page, and everything that is there has been chosen. Space is the material.
styles.philosophy: Confidence is what you leave out. One image, one sentence, an enormous amount of air.
dos: Let one image carry a whole band
donts: Never fill the space you just made
Avoid more than one weight of emphasis

styles.name: Modern Heritage
styles.description: A house with a history, set in warm neutrals with fine rules and a serif that has been trusted for a century.
styles.philosophy: Heritage is not nostalgia. Keep the craft signals — rules, small caps, generous measure — and set them in a contemporary grid.
dos: Use a fine rule where others would use a box
Set body copy at a reading measure

styles.name: Editorial Luxury
styles.description: Fashion-magazine composition: oversized display type crossing full-bleed imagery, asymmetric throughout.
styles.philosophy: Luxury can be loud if it is loud in one register. Enormous type against photography, and nothing else competing.
dos: Let the headline cross the image
donts: Avoid a second loud element in the same band

styles.name: Dark Prestige
styles.description: Near-black ground, a single metallic accent used sparingly, and photography lit like a product still.
styles.philosophy: Darkness makes one thing precious. The accent appears perhaps three times on the whole page and each time it means something.
dos: Use the metallic three times, not thirty
Light the photography like an object
donts: Never lift the canvas to mid-grey
Avoid borders on a dark ground

styles.name: Gallery Luxury
styles.description: Museum discipline applied to a commercial page: white walls, hung work, and captions that know their place.
styles.philosophy: Treat the product as an exhibit. The page is the wall, not the frame, and the caption never shouts over the piece.
dos: Hang the work with space around it
donts: Avoid motion that competes with the work

styles.name: Contemporary Magazine
styles.description: A modern feature well: multi-column text, pull quotes and photography that runs to the margin.
styles.philosophy: Pages that are read, not scanned. Give the words a measure they deserve and let the pictures interrupt at the right moments.
dos: Use a pull quote to change pace
donts: Never let a headline run to 20 words
Avoid card grids where prose belongs

styles.name: Swiss Editorial
styles.description: Grid, flush-left sans, and nothing decorative. Information design applied to a marketing page.
styles.philosophy: The grid does the work. Hierarchy comes from size and position only, never from ornament or colour.

styles.name: Culture Journal
styles.description: A small-press feel: warm paper, generous leading, and imagery treated as plates rather than banners.
styles.philosophy: Written for people who will finish the sentence. Warmth in the paper, patience in the rhythm.
dos: Treat images as plates with captions
donts: Never run text edge to edge

styles.name: Oversized Editorial
styles.description: Display type at poster scale, set against very little else, with words doing the composing.
styles.philosophy: If the sentence is the idea, set it at the size of the idea. Everything else steps back.
dos: Let the headline be the picture
Keep the rest of the band nearly empty
donts: Never add a photograph to compete

styles.name: Newsroom Modern
styles.description: Dense, dated, hierarchical — a front page that assumes there is a lot to say today.
styles.philosophy: Volume is the point. Many stories, ranked clearly, with rules doing the separating.
donts: Never leave a band with one item

styles.name: Executive Precision
styles.description: Boardroom clarity: navy and ink, tight columns, numbers stated plainly.
styles.philosophy: Written for someone with ten minutes. Structure first, proof second, nothing ornamental.
donts: Avoid motion on a proof band

styles.name: Human Corporate
styles.description: Institutional structure warmed by real photography of people and softer surfaces.
styles.philosophy: Large organisations are still made of people. Keep the rigour, lose the coldness.
dos: Show real people doing real work
Soften surfaces without losing the grid

styles.name: Financial Authority
styles.description: Dense, data-led and conservative: tables, figures and a restrained single accent.
styles.philosophy: Money is trusted where nothing is hidden. Show the numbers at full density and let precision persuade.
dos: Keep one accent for the single action
donts: Never illustrate a number with a photograph

styles.name: Global Consulting
styles.description: Wide, systematic, and evidence-heavy, with a cool palette and a strong horizontal rhythm.
styles.philosophy: Breadth is the proposition. Show many capabilities in a legible system rather than one story.
dos: Group capabilities so breadth is scannable
donts: Never lead with one narrow story

styles.name: Institutional Modern
styles.description: Civic weight: stone neutrals, a serif masthead and architecture-led photography.
styles.philosophy: Institutions endure. Materials and proportion say so before any sentence does.
dos: Photograph the building and the work

styles.name: Product Editorial
styles.description: Catalogue as magazine: products photographed as stories, set in a generous editorial grid.
styles.philosophy: People buy the world around the object. Photograph the world, then name the object.
donts: Never show a six-across grid of cut-outs

styles.name: Bold Retail
styles.description: Loud, saturated and fast: big type, strong blocks and an offer you cannot miss.
styles.philosophy: Retail attention lasts a second. Say the offer at full volume and repeat it.
dos: Put the offer above the fold and again at the end
Use the accent at full strength

styles.name: Premium Commerce
styles.description: Considered retail: dark accents on warm neutrals, one product per band, quiet urgency.
styles.philosophy: Premium sells by making the decision feel unhurried. Fewer things, better lit.
dos: Show one product at a time

styles.name: Lifestyle Shop
styles.description: Friendly and bright: rounded surfaces, people in the pictures and a soft secondary colour.
styles.philosophy: The shop is a place you like being. Warmth first, product second.

styles.name: Conversion Minimal
styles.description: One path, no distractions: a single column, one action repeated, everything else removed.
styles.philosophy: Every element that is not the action is competing with it. Remove the competition.
donts: Never add a second competing path

styles.name: Boutique Escape
styles.description: A small property with a point of view: warm sand tones, intimate photography, unhurried pacing.
styles.philosophy: Small places sell intimacy. Show rooms and corners, not lobbies and logos.

styles.name: Resort Editorial
styles.description: Wide horizons and cool light: full-bleed landscape imagery with restrained type laid over it.
styles.philosophy: The place is the product. Give the horizon the full width and stay out of the way.

styles.name: Culinary Luxury
styles.description: Dark, close-lit food photography with a fine serif and almost no chrome.
styles.philosophy: Appetite comes from light on a surface. Darken everything else.
dos: Light the plate, darken the room
donts: Avoid grids of small food images

styles.name: Urban Hotel
styles.description: City confidence: crisp neutrals, architectural photography and a tighter, more functional rhythm.
styles.philosophy: A city guest is booking a base, not a retreat. Be handsome and efficient.
dos: Photograph the building and the street
Make booking the obvious next step

styles.name: Organic Retreat
styles.description: Earth greens and stone, soft edges, and photography of landscape and material.
styles.philosophy: Calm is made from natural material and slow rhythm. Nothing sharp, nothing loud.
donts: Never use a hard square corner

styles.name: Performance Machine
styles.description: Near-black, high-contrast and fast: the machine full-bleed, figures stated like telemetry.
styles.philosophy: Performance is proved by numbers next to a photograph of the thing. Both at full scale.
dos: Run the machine to both edges

styles.name: Grand Touring
styles.description: Long-distance luxury: warm dark neutrals, a serif display and landscape photography.
styles.philosophy: Touring is about the journey. Slower pacing, warmer light, more horizon.
dos: Photograph the road as much as the car

styles.name: Technical Automotive
styles.description: Engineering-forward: exploded diagrams, monospace annotation and a measured grid.
styles.philosophy: For buyers who read the spec sheet first. Show the mechanism, annotate it, do not romanticise it.

styles.name: Heritage Garage
styles.description: Workshop warmth: oil-and-paper neutrals, a condensed display and archival photography.
styles.philosophy: Made by hand, over time. The page should feel like a workshop wall, not a configurator.

styles.name: Future Mobility
styles.description: Clean electric optimism: bright surfaces, soft gradients and generous rounded geometry.
styles.philosophy: New mobility sells calm, not noise. Light, quiet surfaces and a great deal of space.

styles.name: Clinical Calm
styles.description: Cool, orderly and reassuring: pale blues, clear lists and nothing that raises the pulse.
styles.philosophy: An anxious reader needs order. Short bands, plain language, obvious next step.
dos: Answer the worry before the sell

styles.name: Human Wellness
styles.description: Warm and personal: sand and clay tones, rounded surfaces and photography of people.
styles.philosophy: Care is a relationship. Show faces, soften every edge, write in the second person.

styles.name: Premium Medical
styles.description: Private-practice polish: deep neutrals, a serif display and very controlled photography.
styles.philosophy: Expertise at a price should look composed. Fewer claims, better set.

styles.name: Natural Health
styles.description: Botanical and calm: greens and stone, soft shapes, imagery of plants and light.
styles.philosophy: Natural credibility is built from material and restraint, not from claims.
donts: Never make a medical claim look like a slogan

styles.name: Precision Health
styles.description: Data-led medicine: clean white ground, a technical accent and numbers doing the persuading.
styles.philosophy: Evidence is the pitch. Present it like a study, not a brochure.

styles.name: Portfolio Minimal
styles.description: The work, a caption, and nothing else. A studio index rather than a marketing page.
styles.philosophy: A portfolio persuades by sequence, not by argument. Show the work in the right order and stop talking.

styles.name: Art Gallery
styles.description: White walls, fine rules, quiet navigation and artwork given the whole room.
styles.philosophy: The room exists for the work. Everything the page adds must be smaller than what it frames.
dos: Hang the work with air around it
Use a hairline rule instead of a box
donts: Avoid animation that competes with the work

styles.name: Studio Bold
styles.description: A studio with opinions: heavy display type, flat colour blocks and confident asymmetry.
styles.philosophy: A studio should show taste by taking a position. Big type, hard colour, no hedging.
dos: Let type block out the band

styles.name: Cultural Experimental
styles.description: Programme-poster energy: overlapping layers, rotated type and a palette that argues with itself.
styles.philosophy: Cultural work is allowed to be difficult. Layer, overlap, and let the eye find its own route.
donts: Never resolve into a neat grid

styles.name: Motion Creative
styles.description: Built around movement: sequenced reveals, video-first bands and type that arrives.
styles.philosophy: If the studio's craft is motion, the site has to move. Every band earns its animation.
dos: Use video where a still would undersell

styles.name: Neo Brutalist
styles.description: Raw structure on show: black rules, hard shadows, unmodulated colour and no rounding at all.
styles.philosophy: Honesty about the medium. Boxes are boxes, links look like links, nothing pretends to be a material it is not.

styles.name: Retro Future
styles.description: Eighties optimism rebuilt: chrome-adjacent gradients, grid horizons and a saturated duotone.
styles.philosophy: Nostalgia for a future that never arrived. Use its grammar without becoming a pastiche.
donts: Never add a third loud hue

styles.name: Digital Aurora
styles.description: Soft mesh gradients drifting behind pale type, with everything slightly out of focus.
styles.philosophy: Atmosphere as the message. Colour fields do the work that photography usually would.
dos: Let the gradient be the image

styles.name: Geometric System
styles.description: Bauhaus grammar: flat primaries, circles and quadrants used as structure rather than decoration.
styles.philosophy: Shape carries meaning. A small set of forms and colours, repeated with discipline.
dos: Repeat a small set of shapes
donts: Never blur or gradient a shape

styles.name: Typographic Maximalist
styles.description: Type everywhere, at every scale: the page is set rather than laid out.
styles.philosophy: Words are the material. Let scale, weight and density do everything an image would.
dos: Set the page like a poster
Use scale as the only hierarchy
